title: Access
description: Databases and other TCP services stay private. Connect opens a bridge on this machine only, on a free port.

bridges.title: Open bridges
bridges.description: Each bridge binds 127.0.0.1 on a port the kernel picks, so nothing has to give up 5432.
bridges.emptyHint:
Open one from the list below, or from the CLI: portta access open --project

--service
bridges.credentialsHint: credentials come from the project, not from here

services.title: TCP services
services.descriptionEnabled: Reached by hostname where the protocol allows it, and by a temporary loopback bridge everywhere else.
services.descriptionDisabled: Nothing here is published permanently: a bridge exists only while you need it.
services.tlsRequiredHostname: TLS required, and the client must send the hostname
services.serverSpeaksFirst: the server speaks first, so there is no hostname to route on
services.addTcpOverlay: add the TCP overlay to this project

connection.templateHint: credentials come from the project, not from here

forwarders.title: Published on the VPN
forwarders.description: Persistent forwarders created with portta service publish --private.

sites.title: Sites
sites.description: Who may open each address on this host. A decision applies on the next request; nothing restarts.
sites.shownOnce: It appears only now. Give it to whoever needs access.
sites.footPublic: Domain, TLS and VPN are in Settings.
sites.footLocal: On this profile addresses answer only where the gateway can be reached, so there is no decision to take. Domain, TLS and VPN are in Settings.

tcp.passwordFromProject: The password comes from your project; Portta could not read it here.
tcp.notOptedIn: Not enabled for this project: add the TCP overlay to get one.
tcp.routingOff: Hostname routing is off on this host (PORTTA_TCP=false).
tcp.orphans: Their service is gone, but they still hold a port.
